name: Consensus
tagline: AI search engine for scientific research
description: Consensus is an AI research tool for finding answers in scientific papers. Its pricing page lists Individual plus Team and Enterprise options.
limitations: The pricing page we read showed Monthly and Annual toggles but no prices

plans.name: Free
limits: Up to 3 Deep reviews per month

plans.name: Pro

limits: 500 API and MCP uses per month, then $0.05 per use up to 1,000

plans.name: Deep
plans.note: $65 billed monthly, or $540 billed annually ($45 a month equivalent).
limits: 2,000 API and MCP uses per month, then $0.05 per use up to 10,000

plans.name: Team and Enterprise
plans.note: Separate tab on the pricing page; not read.

profile.headline: A search engine for scientific papers that gives answers with the evidence behind them

capabilities.title: Search a very large body of research
capabilities.text: Search covers more than 400 million scientific papers.

capabilities.title: Get a synthesised answer
capabilities.text: Pro Search and Deep Search return AI answers built from the papers they found.

capabilities.title: See how much researchers agree
capabilities.text: The Consensus Meter shows the level of scientific agreement on yes/no questions.

capabilities.title: Question a single paper
capabilities.text: Ask Paper lets you chat with any paper.

featureCards.name: Study Snapshots
featureCards.text: Summaries of a study's key findings and methodology.

featureCards.name: Citation Graph
featureCards.text: Shows how papers relate to each other.

featureCards.name: Citation export
featureCards.text: Export references in RIS, BibTeX and CSV.

featureCards.name: Collections
featureCards.text: Organise the papers you collect into a research library.

featureCards.name: Search controls
featureCards.text: Sources, Skills, Deep and Filter controls sit in the search interface.

featureCards.name: Browser support
featureCards.text: Works in Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge.

audienceDetail.who: Anyone checking a yes/no question against research
audienceDetail.text: The Consensus Meter is built for exactly that. The homepage does not name its audience, so these groups follow from the features it lists.
Ask Paper and Study Snapshots help with a single study.
Citation export in RIS, BibTeX and CSV feeds reference managers.

scenarios.title: Test a claim
scenarios.text: Ask a yes/no question and read the Consensus Meter before you rely on it.

scenarios.title: Skim a study
scenarios.text: Open a Study Snapshot to see the findings and methods quickly.

scenarios.title: Follow the citations
scenarios.text: Use the Citation Graph to trace how related papers connect.

scenarios.title: Build a reference list
scenarios.text: Save papers to a collection and export the citations.

gettingStarted.text: The homepage invites you to start your research from the search box.
Use plain wording, or switch to Pro Search or Deep Search.
Read the Study Snapshot, or chat with the paper using Ask Paper.
Add papers to a collection and export citations when you write.
